title: Grace V. Ringlein
text:
I am a fourth year PhD Candidate in Biostatistics at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public health (anticipated graduation in May 2027), advised by Elizabeth Stuart and Trang Nguyen. My research interests broadly include causal inference, electronic health records, algorithmic fairness, and mental health. My dissertation work focuses specifically on the challenge of unobserved confounding.

See my Student Spotlight to read about my experience in the Department of Biostatistics at Johns Hopkins!

title: Grace V. Ringlein
text:
Grace is a PhD Candidate in Biostatistics at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. Her research interests are in causal inference, measurement error, health disparities, and mental health.

title: Grace V. Ringlein
text:
I am a fourth year PhD Candidate in Biostatistics at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public health (anticipated graduation in May 2027), advised by Elizabeth Stuart and Trang Nguyen. My research interests broadly include causal inference, electronic health records, algorithmic fairness, and mental health. My dissertation work focuses specifically on the challenge of unobserved confounding.

See my Student Spotlight to read about my experience in the Department of Biostatistics at Johns Hopkins!
